sections.text: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।
Whenever spirituality decays and materialism is rampant, then, O Arjuna, I reincarnate Myself!
To protect the righteous, to destroy the wicked and to establish the kingdom of God, I am reborn from age to age.
जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः।
He who realises the divine truth concerning My birth and life is not born again; and when he leaves his body, he becomes one with Me.

We had been discussing chapter four, Gnana Karma Sannyasa Yoga, Yoga of Renunciation of Action in Knowledge. We have seen so far that in chapter three, Bhagavan has taught Arjuna Karma Yoga. In that he said that you should perform actions for Yajna Yajnarth Puru Karmani.
Then he also said, asaktah Sattattam Karma Samajaraha. Perform all your actions without attachment. And he said, yogastha Guru Karmani, establish your Sulmi Yoga and they perform your actions.
So these are the three requisites or three path. Three ways of performing actions Bhagavan has indicated to Arjuna and he called it Karma Yoga. How you can continue performing your actions in this world as required by roles you are taken.
The art of performing action called Karma Yoga. Bhagavan Seth was taught to the royal sages, the philosopher kings, right from the beginning. Right from the beginning of the creation.
This knowledge was given to Lord sun, who is considered to be in this case, the original ruler of this universe. He then gave it to his successor. His successor gave it to his successor.
And this knowledge was passed on one royal sage to the another, one philosopher king, to another philosopher king. You know, kings were not just simply the rulers, but they were also established in Dharma. They were established in the knowledge.
But this knowledge was lost over a period of time. And therefore I have given it to you again today, and you shall also be able to use it. But then Arjuna asked, how can that be possible? Because you are under my contemporary, how you could give this knowledge to Lord Son.
And in that response we all learned how the reincarnation works. So Bhagavan said, bahuni me vyati Thani Janma ne tava Charjana. Oh Arjuna, you and I have gone through many, many Janmas, many, many iterations of our existence.
The only difference, he is saying that I know them all and you do not know any. Thats because you take birth. I, as a Jiva, take birth, compelled by my own vasanas.
My unfulfilled desires. I take a new instrument to fulfill my vasanas which I have not fulfilled yet. If I have no vasanas, no desires, there is no reason for me to take birth.
In other words, there is no action required if there is no desire. I dont need to buy a car if I am never going to travel. People in New York City, most of them dont buy car because they are not going to use car.
Its not economical for them to bike. They dont need that equipment. People like us, we need that equipment.
Because there is only way we can travel from one place to another. We have desire to travel. The equipment needed is a car.
Therefore, Ill buy a car. In the same way you are driven by your own vasanas, take another birth. But in my case, there is no need for me.
But I take birth by my own free will because I have a desire. And that is what Bhagavan has basically said. Why he takes that divine birth.
He said, yada yada hi dharmasyagnanir Bhavati Bharata abyuthanam adharmashya tad atmanam srujami ham. The desire may be noble, it may be good or bad. But unless there is desire, there cannot be any action swimming in Bhagavans part also from Ishwaras point of view also he has a desire to set the creation right.
When he sees that the Dharma is declining in his own creation, as we have seen in Vedantic discussions, then Bhagavan creates this universe out of his own self. The Creator is the efficient cause, knows how to create. He also knows how to maintain it.
But the material he used to create this universe, his own self, he has created this universe out of his own self. So he is all pervading in this universe. And he has created this universe out of his own will.
Maya when he sees that his own creation, there is a decay of Dharma. Dharma we have seen in several discussions before is the law of being. That which makes a thing or a being what it is is its Dharma.
If that Dharma is declining, a thing or being is not functioning as it should be, then it needs to be corrected. So here Bhagavan said, when in the society, just as an individual has a Dharma, the society also has a Dharma. Human beings have their own Dharma.
At the basic core level, a human being is a rational animal. He is differentiated from all other animals by his reasoning power. So he can act rationally, he can think rationally.
If human beings stop acting rationally, then Dharma is decayed. If they start acting irrationally, I will say Dharma is decayed for human beings, for that society. So its been current condition, the Dharma of democracy is that everyone has the right to vote or right to give opinion.
When that Dharma is violated, then democracy is decayed and somebody has to come and correct it. So in this case, Bhagavan said, whenever there is a decay of Dharma, when I see that things are not performing as per Dharma, then it has to be replaced, corrected, and the order should be restored. To give you an example from my own observation: the Dharma of a steel beam under a bridge is to provide the tensile strength to that bridge.
Because that beam can bend and come back to its own position -- that is the Dharma of steel. When the steel is corroded, its still steel, but its corroded steel. That steel does not have the tensile strength which was required by that beam, and therefore it needs to be either repaired or replaced.
Whoever is responsible for that bridge may be paying no attention to that beam. But now that he has observed the decay, theres a danger of the bridge collapsing. Well, he has to manifest himself as the corrector for that steel beam.
So he said, yada yada, hi Dharma Siglanir Bhavati. Whenever Dharma has decayed, that things or beings are not acting according to their own Dharma. Abhiuthana Madharma and the rise of Adharma Adharma, which is contrary to his own Dharma.
Human beings are supposed to be rational. They are not acting rationally. They are no different than any other animals.
Society has to be just. If the society is not just, obviously it is not a society. If there is a chaos in the society, whoever is responsible for their society has to restore the order in the society.
It becomes a just society again. Bhagawan said, that is my desire when I take birth by my free will. So we have seen that we are under the spell of Maya.
Therefore, we are deluded by ignorance. Ignorance is veiling my own self. I do not see who I am.
I continue to change my vehicle from this body to another. But thats driven by my vasanas. Ishwara is in control of Maya.
The whole creation is created by his own Maya out of his own self. When he sees this creation is not performing as per his design, he has the desire to set it right. Paritranaya Sadhunam Vinashaya Chaduskritam, Dharma, Sansthapa, Narthaya, Sambhavami, Yuge Yuge.
Time and again I manifest myself as one of my own creation and then set the order correct so that the things which are working as per Dharma are protected, and those which are not acting according to Dharma either need to be corrected, rehabilitated, or replaced. So in the same example of my steel beam under a bridge, there are several steel beams under that bridge. Those are providing the tensile strength to that bridge.
People dont pay much attention. Corroded beams we see all the time. When we see extensive corrosion under that bridge, then whoever is in charge says, We need to do something. Well, lets figure out which beams we can restore and which we have to replace, so that the overall strength of that bridge is restored back to where it should have been.
Dharmasansthapa Narthaya -- for society to function as it was supposed to have functioned, as a just society, then I have to come and restore order: remove those who are poisonous and cannot be rehabilitated, rehabilitate those who can be rehabilitated, so that those who are practicing Dharma are protected and society functions as it was supposed to before the decay started. In verse nine, he says, Arjuna. Here is another method Bhagavan gives us to achieve that state of knowledge.
Right now I am under the spell of Maya and my knowledge is veiled by my ignorance. There are several methods. We have seen Gnana Yoga, Bhakti Yoga, Karma Yoga.
He said that in Karma Yoga, you can perform your actions as we have discussed. Or you can just observe a divine person acting in this world selflessly, recognize how he does it in his divine manifestation, and then find the same divinity within you. You will establish yourself in your own real self, which is your own atma, your own consciousness.
As we have discussed, there is nothing in this world which is not a manifestation of Bhagavan, of Brahman. And therefore you and I cannot be different from Avatara. In our culture we have this Dasha Avatara, but actually thats just the popular version of it.
Some Puranas have 24 Avataras, some have 36. There are numerous descriptions of Avatara, because Avatara means the one who descends -- Avatarati ITI Avatara. You and I also have descended from our highest position of all-knowing self to very limited knowing self.
From these limitations, I want liberation. Bhagavan said, even by observing others, so we create role models in our life, from them we learn. And if I can create the highest role model which has demonstrated how a person established in his own self acts in this world.
Bhagawan said, you can also get liberated just by recognizing how a divine incarnation functions. Janma, Karma, Chame Divyam Evam yo Vittita tv. One who knows in essence what is the purpose of a divine Avatara and how that divine being functions in this world.
Therefore we learn Ramayana, therefore we recite Bhagavad Gita. We are trying to learn from them how Lord Rama acted in his life. If we can understand that, Bhagavan says, then when you give up this body -- if I understood in my life how Rama functioned, what was his motivation to act the way he acted, what was Krishnas motivation -- then I will also find that same self in me through my own contemplation, my own observation of my own self: that this is not me.
The demands of my body, my mind, intellect are not really me. I am something other than that. Having understood this by learning from my own role models, when I give up this body, I dont have to take the birth again.
So in previous descriptions in scriptures, the idea was deathlessness. But then the later portion of our scriptures describes birthlessness instead. Death is obviously something to be afraid of -- therefore dont get infected by coronavirus, social distancing, all of that.
Death is the one thing you are worried about. But somehow we are going to die anyway, coronavirus or no coronavirus. The very thought that I will start all over again -- I have come all this far, from learning ABCD to whatever, went through kindergarten, then high school, then college -- and I have to start all over again.

These verses contain the famous promise of divine intervention: Yada yada hi dharmasya glanir bhavati - whenever Dharma declines and Adharma rises, the Lord manifests to protect the righteous, destroy wickedness, and re-establish Dharma. This is not merely about cosmic events but applies to our inner life as well. Just as a gardener tolerates a few weeds but eventually must restore order, the divine principle within us rises to correct imbalance when we stray too far from our essential nature.
Dharma here means the law of being - that which makes a thing what it is. When a steel beam loses its tensile strength through corrosion, it has lost its dharma and must be repaired or replaced. Similarly, when we deviate from our own authentic nature, life itself creates situations that call us back to alignment. The teaching also reveals that one who truly understands the divine birth and actions (janma karma cha me divyam) becomes free from the cycle of rebirth. This is not mere intellectual understanding but a profound recognition that transforms ones entire being.
Today, examine where in your life Dharma may be declining - where are you not functioning according to your true nature? What corrective forces have appeared to guide you back? Also reflect: Bhagavan says He comes paritranaya sadhunam - to protect those practicing Dharma. What good thoughts or intentions within you need protection from being overwhelmed by negative tendencies? Trust that when you sincerely seek to follow Dharma, the inner voice of guidance will strengthen and rise to support you. The goal is birthlessness (aja) - to exhaust all desires so completely that no new birth is needed.
